title: Cost Conservation: Incremental Bundles for Real-time LLM Serving
creator: Priya Ramesh
description:
Objective: Drive a 20-30% reduction in per-token serving cost for real-time chat and completion workloads by rolling out small, reversible bundles of optimizations (micro-batching + targeted KV caching + conservative quantization) across progressively larger customer cohorts.

Context: We've validated each knob in isolation (lab benchmarks show batching and KV cache synergy, and int4 quant yields 1.2-1.6x throughput for selected models). Customers require predictable latency SLOs and no measurable quality regressions. This initiative defines the runway, rollout gates, and OKR metrics to move from experiments to product-safe rollouts.

Scope: Pilot with two mid-sized customers and internal traffic lanes, implement rollout orchestration in Console for canaries, integrate cost telemetry to the Serving Economics dashboard, and formalize QA/rollback playbooks. Work is confined to hosted API and Dedicated for initial phase; Private will follow after validation.

Why incremental bundles? Separating the knobs into small bundles (e.g., batch+cache, cache+int4, batch+int4) reduces blast radius and lets us attribute savings and quality impact precisely. The approach also enables quicker operational adoption and customer opt-in mechanics in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Field trials demonstrate >=15% token-cost reduction for non-high-precision workloads and >=20% in aggregate across pilot cohorts
No quality regression >1% on core evaluation suites (intent preservation, hallucination rate) for canary traffic
End-to-end canary orchestration available in Console with clear rollback, concurrency limits, and per-customer opt-in toggles
Cost telemetry integrated with per-route token breakdowns and alerting on anomaly (>10% deviation vs baseline)
Runbook for incidentability and postmortem template completed and approved by SRE

2025-02-20: Lab experiments complete. Observed: batch(20ms)+kv gives 12-18% savings; int4 adds marginal 6-10% but has model-specific quality sensitivity on long-context prompts.

2025-03-05: Quality threshold tests show <0.6% drift on short-forms; long-format drift at 1.3% for a small subset when int4 enabled — decided to hold int4 for long-context until model-specific QA completes. Updated plan accordingly.
decisions: Adopt 'bundle-first' rollout: release additive bundles in sequence to minimize attribution ambiguity
Initial batching window target: 20ms for low-latency lanes, 50ms for best-effort lanes; dynamic backoff if tail latencies >SLO
Quantization policy: expose int8 for pilots; int4 gated and applied only to short-context models after per-model QA pass
KV cache TTL: tiered TTLs (30s/2m/10m) by route class; experiments will determine hit-rate sweet-spot
Customer opt-in required for any change that could touch data residency or KMS-protected models
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions for long-context when combining int4 + aggressive batching. Mitigation: hold int4 in long-context; run additional long-form evals and narrow int4 to specific model shards.

Risk: Unexpected tail-latency spikes after enabling batching. Mitigation: introduce concurrency caps, monitor p99 and register automatic rollback at threshold, and run chaos tests before wider rollout.
Risk: Difficulty attributing savings. Mitigation: staggered A/B windows, per-route token accounting, and synthetic traffic baselines to isolate noise.
